name: Ab wheel rollout
pattern: Dynamic anti-extension: the arms roll a wheel, ball or bar forward so the body lengthens toward the floor, then the abs and lats pull it back.
setup: Kneel on a pad, hands on the wheel under your shoulders.
Tuck your tailbone slightly and brace; back flat to a little rounded.

steps.text: Roll the wheel forward as the hips follow, body getting longer and lower.
Stop just before your low back starts to sag.
Pull the wheel back toward your knees with straight arms, hips last.

cues.cue: Keep the slight tuck; never let the back sag.
cues.why: The rollout is one of the highest abdominal exercises measured, because the abs must stop spine extension.

cues.cue: Only go as far as you can keep the tuck.
cues.why: The lever grows as you go out; partial range is fine.

cues.cue: Straight arms; pull back with the lats.
cues.why: Latissimus dorsi activity was high in rollouts.
Leaving the hips behind turns it into a shoulder stretch.

breathing: Breathe in on the way out, out as you roll back.

tempo.note: Roll out in 2 s, pause, roll back in 2 s.

mistakes.name: Low back sags
mistakes.looks: At full reach the hips drop and the back arches.
mistakes.fix: Shorten the range; tuck the tailbone.
mistakes.why: Load moves from the abs to the spine.

mistakes.name: Hips stay back
mistakes.looks: Only the arms reach forward; hips stay over the knees.
mistakes.fix: Let hips travel forward with the wheel.
mistakes.why: The trunk lever never lengthens, so the abs barely work.

mistakes.name: Bending the elbows
mistakes.looks: Elbows bend and the move becomes a push-up.
mistakes.fix: Lock the elbows; move from the shoulders.
mistakes.why: It shortens the lever and shifts work to the chest and triceps.

safety: Low back pain: start on a stability ball or roll toward a wall to limit range.
Shoulder pain: shorten the range; avoid going past arms overhead.

variants.change: Forearms on a ball: easier, still among the best abdominal exercises.
Roll toward a wall to cap the range.
From standing: very hard; the whole body becomes the lever.
Forearm plank with feet on a slider or straps, rocking forward and back.
Hands in straps: unstable and adjustable by body angle.
Roll out on a diagonal: more oblique work.

subtypes.name: Body saw
subtypes.change: Forearm plank with feet on a slider or ball; push the body back and pull forward.

subtypes.name: Stability ball rollout
subtypes.change: Kneel, forearms on the ball; roll it forward until arms are near overhead.

motion.basis: Kneeling wheel rollout. All angles estimated from the technique; activation findings from escamilla2006, escamilla2010 and youdas2008.

sources.cite: Escamilla RF et al. Electromyographic analysis of traditional and nontraditional abdominal exercises: implications for rehabilitation and training. Phys Ther. 2006;86(5):656-671.
Escamilla RF, Lewis C, Bell D, et al. Core muscle activation during Swiss ball and traditional abdominal exercises. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther. 2010;40(5):265-276.

McGill S, Andersen J, Cannon J. Muscle activity and spine load during anterior chain whole body linkage exercises: the body saw, hanging leg raise and walkout from a push-up. J Sports Sci. 2015;33(4):419-426.
